Scope: Python install manager and official CPython runtime acquisition source review

Msix.PublisherPageNotes: Bundles Python 3.15.0 for x64 and ARM64; official page reports 96.2 MB.

Msi.PublisherPageNotes: Official page reports 10.3 MB and says to consult advanced-installation documentation.

Constraints: Publisher recommends Store/MSIX; python.org and Store MSIX variants cannot be installed together.
MSI is a per-machine installation to Program Files and attempts to modify system PATH.
Runtimes managed by the manager remain per-user, including when the manager MSI is machine-wide.
The manager automatically updates within a day of a release; no supported disable control was found in the reviewed documentation.
The traditional full installer is deprecated since Python 3.14 and will not be produced starting with Python 3.16.
Manager supports Windows 10 and Windows Server 2022 or later.

AcceptedPolicyMechanics.DisableImplicitRuntimeInstallation: Set automatic_install=false in the per-user %AppData%\Python\pymanager.json configuration; publisher documentation states the default is true.
AcceptedPolicyMechanics.ExplicitRuntimeSelection: Use exact tags such as 3.15.1-64; the manager supports explicit install commands.
AcceptedPolicyMechanics.OfflinePreparation: Use py install --download to create an offline index, then py install --source=<local index> on the target.
AcceptedPolicyMechanics.RuntimeUpdates: py install --update is an explicit runtime-update command and updates can change installed packages.

EvidenceLimits.Consequence: The SHA-256 values are publisher-manifest values, not locally verified artifact hashes; candidates remain unregistered and unsupported.

Deferred: Acquire and rehash pinned manager/runtime artifacts
Define manager auto-update and conflicting python/py aliases behavior
Implement exact user config and offline index ownership/recovery
Test runtime selection, no implicit download, offline installation, separate update, and recovery on disposable Windows
Partial: InstallPython retains selected manager and traditional routes; no Python package candidate or runtime policy handler exists.
